Implement internal-hook dispatcher: real commits now get identity

Closes HANDOFF.md known-issue #1: `git for-ai init` installed hooks that
dispatched to a `git-for-ai internal-hook` command that didn't exist, so
real commits got no Change-Id trailer and no change-map entry (identity
only existed via capture-session's R5 orphan-recovery fallback).

New command (hidden from --help), dispatching per ARCHITECTURE.md:
- commit-msg: injects `Change-Id: I<32hex>` into the message file via
  `git interpret-trailers --in-place` (verified: lands before comments
  and the `commit -v` scissors section) — §7.2's before-SHA injection.
  Guards: no-op when a trailer already exists (Gerrit coexistence §7.6)
  and when the effective message is empty (injecting there would turn
  an aborted commit into a trailer-only commit).
- post-commit: assignChangeId(HEAD) — adopts the injected trailer.
- post-rewrite: parsePostRewriteInput(stdin) + onPostRewrite (§7.4).

Same hard rule as capture-session: the bin.ts wrapper always exits 0,
logging failures to .git-for-ai/hooks.log (stderr fallback) so a hook
can never break a user's git operation.

Also: package-level vitest configs for cli and core setting the 60s
test timeout globally — log/show/init test files never carried the
per-file vi.setConfig the other git-heavy suites had, and flaked under
full-parallel `turbo test` subprocess load (2 timeouts at the 5s
default). 12 new tests; 276 total, all passing.

Implemented inline by the orchestrating session (Fable 5).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
